narrative: This snapshot follows a 41-day gap in the daily refresh (last run 2026-06-13; the systemd timer resumed 2026-07-23), so day-over-day deltas below aren't meaningful — treat this as a fresh baseline. Over that span the bridge kept growing (custody +32% to 1.02M PRL) and block production diversified away from MinePRL, which has gone offline, to at least six independent pools (PearlHash, Kryptex, Pearl Fortune, Hero Miners, LuckyPool, AlphaPool). Separately, a July 1 PoW extension (MoE support) turned out to be economically mispriced, letting reported hashrate balloon before the core team shipped a same-day consensus fork fix — full detail in incidents below. GitHub cadence has cooled to 7 commits across tracked repos this week, consistent with a project past its initial sprint.

anomalies: This run follows a 41-day gap since the last daily refresh (2026-06-13 → 2026-07-24); the timer that wakes this agent stopped and only resumed 2026-07-23. Custody grew from 771,308 to 1,019,200 PRL (+32%) over that span — healthy multi-week bridge growth, not a single-day swing, so the usual >20%/day check doesn't apply cleanly this run.

The relay's /api/supply endpoint (1,009,389.69 PRL) reads 126 PRL higher than /api/custody's totalSupplyGrains (1,009,263.69 PRL); this persisted across a retry two seconds apart, so it isn't a mid-update race. Both custody-side counters (totalCustodyGrains and mintedGrains) agree internally. Worth a look, not urgent.
Zero mints/burns via the intermediary path in the last 24h and 7d; all recent flow is direct mint/burn.
Fast-lane usage reads 0% because this snapshot lands moments after the daily UTC window reset — same pattern as prior runs, not a usage drop.

social.summary: Pearlbridge's own account kept up its developer-education cadence (decimals handling, gas-token mechanics). The dominant story this week was the Pearl L1 PoW/consensus issue described in incidents below — community sentiment on it ranged from alarmed ("Pearl may have a HUGE problem") to reassured once the DeFiLlama hack-list came back clean and the core team's fix merged. Outside of that, most "$PRL" volume in the raw mention count is unrelated noise: a distinct "Perle Labs" project sharing the PRL ticker, a Pakistan Stock Exchange ticker (PRL), and generic uses of the word "pearl."

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.
